qa.question: Is Rio Grande unit 7 still due to retire in 2027?
qa.finding: The commission's final order of April 4, 2025 allows El Paso Electric to abandon unit 7 and hold it in contingency reserve until it is retired. The EIA table for September 2026 still lists unit 7 as operating with a planned retirement in December 2027.
qa.recommendation: Leave the status as operating and the planned retirement as 2027. Ask the project manager whether the unit should be marked mothballed once El Paso Electric reports it in contingency reserve.
qa.note:
Opened the case notice at https://epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/notice-for-23-00403-ut.pdf (page 1, paragraph 1, asks to abandon Rio Grande unit 7 and Newman unit 1 by January 1, 2026) and a New Mexico Political Report article at https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2025/03/06/el-paso-electric-wants-to-replace-aging-natural-gas-generation-with-renewables/ (says the commission did not vote and the chairman said it will likely be approved). I could not find the commission's final order; the commission's case guest index did not show the case in the earlier harvest.

Final order:
- Open El Paso Electric's 2025 resource plan at https://www.epelectric.com/files/24-00260-UT-2025-09-02-EPE-Integrated-Resource-Plan-Report.pdf and go to the footnote 11 under Table 34 at the page printed as 114. It says 'Per the Commission's Final Order, EPE may abandon RG7 and Newman 1 according to the plan submitted in its Application' and cites 'Final Order Granting Abandonment, Ordering Paragraph B (Apr. 4, 2025)'.
- The same plan's Table 34 lists Rio Grande 7 with accredited capacity of 0 MW.
- I could not open the order itself because the commission's case pages are drawn by scripts and the order has no address of its own.

qa.question: Should the 2026 planned retirement on Rio Grande unit 6 be cleared?
qa.finding: Unit 6 is shown as retired in September 2025 by both the EIA table and El Paso Electric's plan, so the 2026 planned retirement no longer applies.
qa.recommendation: After the status change to retired is accepted, ask the project manager to clear the Planned retire value of 2026 and set Retired year to 2025.
qa.note: Sources are the EIA table at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (Retired sheet, plant 2444, generator 6) and the plan at https://www.epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/2026_epe_system_expansion_plan_2027-2036.pdf (PDF page 17, note 2).

qa.question: What was the 'Rio Grande CT G10' of 87 MW that was terminated?
qa.finding: I found no public document that names a Rio Grande unit 10. The EIA table for September 2026 lists only generators 6, 7, 8 and 9 at plant 2444, and El Paso Electric's 2026 plan lists only G6 to G9.
qa.recommendation: Do not add a unit. Leave GEM as is unless the project manager finds a document naming a unit 10.
qa.note: I checked https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (all sheets, plant 2444) and https://www.epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/2026_epe_system_expansion_plan_2027-2036.pdf (PDF page 17). The 87 MW size is close to the 88 MW shown for unit 9 in the plan, so it may be an early name for unit 9. I could not confirm that.
